root_cause.text: The Rust Binder `thread.rs` fixup handling incorrectly used `skip == 0` as a sentinel for “write a pointer fixup,” so an empty `binder_fd_array_object` with zero fds was misclassified and led `apply_sg()` to perform an out-of-bounds 8-byte write at the end of the buffer.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states that “an empty FDA (fd array) object with 0 fds would cause an out-of-bounds error” because “the previous implementation used `skip == 0` to mean ‘this is a pointer fixup’, but 0 is also the correct skip length for an empty FDA,” and the diff replaces the `PointerFixupEntry { skip: 0, pointer_value, target_offset }` pattern with an explicit `enum PointerFixupEntry::{Fixup, Skip}` in `drivers/android/binder/thread.rs`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Replace the implicit skip-versus-fixup struct encoding with an explicit enum to make pointer fixup handling clearer and safer.
intent_record.what: The `PointerFixupEntry` type was changed from a single struct with three fields (`skip`, `pointer_value`, `target_offset`) into an enum with two variants: `Fixup { pointer_value, target_offset }` for `binder_buffer_object` fixups and `Skip { skip, target_offset }` for `binder_fd_array_object` skips. The surrounding documentation comments were updated to match the new representation.
intent_record.how: This change makes the two logical cases explicit in the type system instead of encoding them implicitly with a `skip == 0` convention. At runtime, code using this type can now distinguish pointer writes from skip entries more safely and clearly, reducing the chance of misinterpreting an entry or applying the wrong kind of fixup.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use the explicit `Fixup` variant when recording pointer fixups instead of a struct entry with `skip: 0`.
intent_record.what: In `translate_object`, the code that pushes a `PointerFixupEntry` into `parent_entry.pointer_fixups` was changed from constructing a struct literal with `skip: 0` plus `pointer_value` and `target_offset` to constructing the enum variant `PointerFixupEntry::Fixup { pointer_value, target_offset }`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this changes how the pointer fixup is represented in the fixup list: instead of encoding a fixup as a generic entry with an explicit zero skip field, it now records it as a dedicated `Fixup` variant. This likely makes the translation logic interpret the entry as a real pointer fixup rather than relying on a default skip value.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use the explicit Skip fixup variant when translating the object so skipped pointer data is handled correctly.
intent_record.what: The code changes the pushed fixup record from constructing a `PointerFixupEntry` with fields `skip: fds_len`, `pointer_value: 0`, and `target_offset: info.target_offset` to constructing a `PointerFixupEntry::Skip { skip: fds_len, target_offset: info.target_offset }` enum variant.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the code now records this case as an explicit skip-type pointer fixup instead of a generic entry with a zero pointer value. This likely changes how later fixup processing interprets the record, preventing the skipped region from being treated as a real pointer and making the intent of skipping `fds_len` bytes explicit.

intent_record.intent_summary: Correct pointer fixup handling by distinguishing fixup and skip variants and validating bounds against the proper target offset.
intent_record.what: The code handling `sg_entry.pointer_fixups` was changed from using `fixup.skip` with an implicit special case when `skip == 0` to matching on `PointerFixupEntry` variants. `Fixup` now always uses `size_of::<u64>()` and its `target_offset`, while `Skip` uses its explicit `skip` and `target_offset`. The subsequent bounds checks and warning message were updated to use the new `fixup_offset` variable instead of `fixup.target_offset`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, pointer fixup processing now distinguishes between fixup entries that represent a real pointer write and entries that represent a skip. This makes the computed length and target offset reflect the entry type directly, preventing incorrect interpretation of zero-length or zero-skip cases and ensuring the out-of-bounds validation is performed against the correct offset.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix scatter-gather fixup handling to copy the correct range and write pointer values at the proper offset only for real fixup entries.
intent_record.what: The code changes the copy length calculation from `fixup.target_offset - end_of_previous_fixup` to `fixup_offset - end_of_previous_fixup`, and replaces the `if fixup.skip == 0` write condition with a pattern match on `PointerFixupEntry::Fixup { pointer_value, .. }`, writing `pointer_value` at `fixup_offset` instead of `fixup.target_offset`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now copies the correct number of bytes up to the current fixup offset and only performs the pointer write for entries that are actually fixups. This prevents writing based on the old target_offset/skip logic and aligns the pointer insertion with the computed fixup position, avoiding incorrect offsets or skipped writes when processing scatter-gather fixups.
